item.title: Algeria
item.description:
About

Algeria features a diverse landscape that includes mountain ranges, vast deserts, and karstic plateaus, making it highly relevant from a speleological and geological perspective.

🪨 Limestone Karst in Algeria

Yes, Algeria has significant limestone karst formations, especially in the northern and northeastern regions of the country. These include:

  • Djurdjura Mountains (part of the Tell Atlas): This region has well-developed karst plateaus with numerous caves and sinkholes, formed in Jurassic and Cretaceous limestones.
  • **Constantine and Setif regions**: Known for complex karst systems and underground hydrology.
  • Tassili n’Ajjer (southeastern Algeria - DO NOT TRAVEL): While primarily known for its sandstone formations and prehistoric rock art, some karst-like erosion features occur in isolated carbonate outcrops.

item.title: Allendale East Cave – Soggy Wombats
item.description:
Allendale East Cave

Introduction

Known as the hole in the middle of the road or just ‘the Dale’, Allendale East Cave is a very popular site among the CDAA Cave rated divers in the Mount Gambier region. As it presents itself as a non-complex cave to dive in, the Soggy Wombats Team has been training, developing skills and accumulating experience in this cave since 2019. Although geographically far from the most developed cave systems in the region, ‘the Dale’ has a small ‘tunnel’ at it’s deepest end that has been in most of Australian’s Cave Divers dreams to break into something big. There hasn’t been any breakthrough in this cave in the last 20 years or so, but with the advances in exploration techniques, we might be surprised with what the future will tell us.

item.title: Article - Corra-Lynn
item.description: When I tell people I’ve just met that I’m a cave diver with claustrophobia, I always get a few confused looks followed by an inevitable round of questions along the lines of “Oh, so how do you stop the panic then?”. But when I mention my claustrophobia to people who know me and the kind of cave diving I do, the reaction is generally more like “You are very clearly broken, Josh - what is wrong with your brain?”.

item.title: Article - Iddlebiddy Cave - Soggy Wombats - DRAFT
item.description:
Introduction

First discovered sometime in the early 1980’s by an enthusiastic band of unqualified local divers, Iddlebiddy Cave was named as a tongue-in-cheek nod to far larger Cocklebiddy Cave on the Nullarbor Plains which is resembles in structure if not in size. The location of Iddlebiddy Cave remained a closely guarded secret for several years, until it was first formally surveyed on 26 November 1988 by Tony Hambling, Frank Homewood and John McCormick on behalf of the Cave Divers Association of Australia.

item.title: Cocklebiddy Cave - 6N48
item.description:
About

Cocklebiddy Cave is over 6.5km long and is the longest single underwater passage in Australia. The entrance is in a degraded doline 120m long and a steep talus slope beneath overhang at the North end leads to large chamber 360 x 45 x 30m high with 180m long lake. The lake contains “mud islands”.

It is possible to snorkel the lake to look down at the first sump, the water can be muddy after rain.

item.title: Goa Lalauwi
item.description:
About

From Anita: - This is a cave that deserves a special mention. A 600m submerged tunnel leads into the heart of the cave. So far around 3km of tunnels have been explored, yet the cave keeps on going. Goa Lalauwi keeps a few secrets up its sleeve as it wants you to come back for more. On my first dive we swam through big tunnels with white limestone, sections of fractured rock and large areas of stalagmites in crystal clear blue water. To get to the water you walk over 100 steps down a dry chamber which means the cave it self is never exposed to any sunlight. It’s pitch black. This means you are reliant on your torch as soon as you step into the cave. It is quite slippery at the entrance lake and you need to take care not to slip and fall. Then you kit up inside the lake aided by your torch light before the descent towards the first tunnel. The second dive in this beauty was far more complex from a navigational perspective with lots of directional decisions and several jumps that lead to a section with little white humps in the form of witches’ hats. According to our guide, these formations are considered quite rare and, unlike the other speleothems in the caves, form under water. While I have spent several hours in this cave, I will be back for more.

item.title: Gua La Pahia
item.description:
To Do

Diving Dry Photogrammetry

About

Description:

“The House Cave” for Kadena Glamping Muna

  • From Anita:
    • “In the backyard of where we stayed lies Goa La Pahia, the hidden cave, with an unassuming small rock entrance surrounded by vegetation. As you descend, it slowly unveils its secrets. Calcite crystal formations decorate the ceiling. which tum into whole sections covered in crystal straws. As you swim further along the cave it reveals more and more of its unique formations. Small but impressive, it has a special place in my heart. The first underwater crystal cave that I have ever seen was a dream come true. The sheer beauty, uniqueness and the masses of speleothems took a while to sink in. I was on such a high, but at the same time I was so calm and close to a meditative state as I took in the surroundings with awe and wonder. This was my introduction to cave diving in Muna Island. What a phenomenal start that made me curious for what lay in store for the coming days.”

item.title: Murra-El-Elevyn - 6N47
item.description:
About

Description: Also known as Cocklebiddy 3 Mile Cave, the entrance is a small overhanging doline 20m in diameter. A 20m pitch leads to a loose talus and silt slope which becomes a boulder floored passage after the doline. The passage continues to a small lake at 89m. There are wetas near the entrance of the cave. There was a thylacine carcase found on early trips to the cave.

Uphill of the lake leads to further boulder floored chambers with bats. There are 300m of low maze passages beyond the lake, which contains gypsum flowers and needles. The cave breathes in maze section.

item.title: Photogrammetry
item.description:
Processing

  • Grace Cave
  • LiDAR of Reynella Cave

Ideas

  • Photogrammetry - Rig Setup For a dedicated Windows photogrammetry box:
  • Install NVIDIA Studio Drivers (not Game Ready)
  • Disable Windows sleep/hibernation
  • Set Power Plan to High Performance
  • Exclude project folders from Windows Defender scanning
  • Disable automatic reboots for updates
  • Put your project cache/scratch on a separate NVMe drive

Other

  • Share models on Soggy Wombats Website

Software

  • Metashape
    • Buy Metashape Pro? & run Metashape Cloud?
  • Reality Capture
    • Free it but can’t do spherical/360 images
  • Postshot
  • Polycam phone app

Data Storage & Processing

  • On-Prem: SSD storage in a NAS (see Gear)
    • Citrix to remotely access home server?
  • Portable: Rugged 2Tb HDD - $130
  • Cloud: AWS with S3 bucket
    • ChatGPT - Remote Photogrammetry with StarLink
    • Use S3 to store final models that display on a website - Stack Overflow
    • Amazon Console - Login
    • ChatGPT - Cloud-Based Photogrammetry]]
    • Run Photogrammetry in the Cloud - AWS How-To <– READ THIS IT’S IMPORTANT
  • Other Cloud: MaxCloudOn is dedicated photogrammetry service with $20 credit
  • belowJS - Sharing cave models

Gear

  • X5 - Wired - X5 Review - X5 replacement lenses ($30)
    • Benefit of X5 having user replaceable lens - scratches from dry caving
    • Dive Case Polish? Autosol 75ml Acrylic Polish TESTED - POOR RESULTS
  • Lighting
    • Third BigBlue VL18000PBRC? $1500AUD (Adreno)
    • BigBlue Remote Control - $150US (From BigBlue)
  • Geolocation
    • Insta360 GPS Remote for $80 from AliExpress
    • Drone - use metadata from photos
  • LiDAR
    • Raven Spatial Scanner - $999USD
      • Don’t get RTK - no GPS inside caves, and GPS fix provided by drone)
      • Don’t need Max version - use X4/5 for high res textures

Other Ideas

  • Improved photogrammetry rig?
    • 4x GoPros on helmet? Concerns about weight/neck strain
    • Clamp two Carbon Fibre Floats
      • 4x triple ball clamps
      • 4x GoPros at the front
      • 3-4x lights at the back
    • Hose Clamps with foam/rubber between?)
  • Is there an exploration/business plan here?

item.title: Tommy Graham's Cave - 6N56
item.description:
About

Description: The entrance to the cave is a large doline 50m in diameter. The obvious route into the doline leads to short cave below the Northwest cliff line.

The main cave has been described as a “wombat- sized hole” which is found in the Southeast end of the doline, about 3m down from the level of the plain. There is a visitor book on a rock shelf in the entrance. The way on is not obvious and goes through a rock squeeze at the end of the low entrance chamber.

item.title: Weebubbie Cave - 6N2
item.description:
About

Description: The entrance to Weebubbie Cave is a large doline 45m in diameter, with a boulder “saddle” at its base. A large main passage with a broken rock floor leads to two lakes at 84m below the surface. The route through the cave is track marked with reflective markers. The cave contains bats and bacterial colonies.

Most visitors spend time at the main lake which has water so clear it is easy to accidently step into the water at the lakes edge. The ridge between the two lakes is a convenient place to change if you are snorkelling the lake. With care, it is possible to see some bacterial colonies under boulders while snorkelling in the smaller, Western lake.
